title: Man dies in RCMP custody in Enfield
subtitle: No altercation between prisoner and officers, RCMP say
article: Halifax police are investigating the death of a 28-year-old man at the Enfield RCMP detachment.
Ryan Allen McKay, 28, from Waverley, was found dead in a holding cell early Sunday, less than seven hours after he was arrested.
The RCMP said McKay was co-operative when he was picked up at a home in Enfield around 9 p.m. Saturday for breaching a court order.
"He was acting very normally. There didn't seem to be any reason for concern as to whether they should be seeking medical attention," said Sgt. Mark Gallagher, spokesman for the RCMP in Nova Scotia.
McKay was placed in an empty cell at the RCMP station to await a court appearance on Monday.
Gallagher said guards checked on McKay throughout the night. Then around 3:30 a.m., they noticed he wasn't responsive. Paramedics were called, but they couldn't revive him.
Gallagher said there were no signs that McKay was drunk or high, or any obvious indications that he killed himself.
There was no altercation between McKay and staff, Gallagher added.
An autopsy was scheduled for Monday.
The Halifax Regional Police have been called in to conduct the investigation, with the help of the RCMP major crime unit.
